name: Rhizomelic Chondrodysplasia Punctata Type 2
aliases: Rhizomelic Chondrodysplasia Punctata, Zellweger Spectrum Disorder Type 2

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Biochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Rhizomelic Chondrodysplasia Punctata

criteria.description: Bilateral shortening of the proximal limbs (rhizomelia)
Presence of punctate calcifications in cartilage visible on radiographs
Biochemical evidence of plasmalogen deficiency in erythrocytes or fibroblasts
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the PEX7 gene
Characteristic facial features including midface hypoplasia and depressed nasal bridge

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of rhizomelia and chondrodysplasia punctata on imaging plus biochemical confirmation of plasmalogen deficiency
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for PEX7 mutations supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and biochemical criteria are met.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Rhizomelic shortening of the humerus and femur
searchTerms: rhizomelic shortening of humerus and femur
proximal limb bones shorter than normal
spots of calcium in growth plate cartilage

pathognomonic.notes: Detected via biochemical assays in erythrocytes or fibroblasts
searchTerms: severe deficiency of plasmalogens causing symptoms
plasmalogen shortage leading to clinical signs

common.symptomName: Facial dysmorphism including midface hypoplasia and depressed nasal bridge
searchTerms: facial features with midface underdevelopment and flat nose
midface hypoplasia with depressed nasal bridge
distinct facial dysmorphism with flat nose

common.symptomName: Cataracts present at birth or early infancy
Severe developmental delay and intellectual disability
Joint contractures and limited range of motion
Growth retardation with failure to thrive

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory distress due to recurrent infections
searchTerms: respiratory distress due to recurrent lung infections

laboratory: Severe deficiency of plasmalogens in erythrocytes and fibroblasts
Elevated phytanic acid and pristanic acid levels
Normal very long chain fatty acids differentiating from Zellweger syndrome
imaging: Radiographic evidence of punctate calcifications in epiphyseal cartilage
Rhizomelic shortening of long bones on X-ray
Brain MRI may show delayed myelination

distinguishingFeatures: PEX7 gene mutations in type 2 vs PEX7 or other peroxisomal genes in type 1
More severe neurological involvement in type 1
Different biochemical profiles including very long chain fatty acid abnormalities in type 1
Diffuse peroxisomal biogenesis defects vs isolated plasmalogen deficiency
More severe multi-organ involvement in Zellweger syndrome
Presence of elevated very long chain fatty acids in Zellweger spectrum

redFlags: Severe rhizomelic limb shortening detected prenatally or at birth
Punctate calcifications in cartilage on radiographs
Marked plasmalogen deficiency on biochemical testing
references: Braverman NE, et al. Rhizomelic Chondrodysplasia Punctata Type 2. GeneReviews. 2020.
